recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. If this behavior regresses, fix it in the current external validator or IG Publisher tooling rather than by editing core StructureDefinition source.
issue_request: FHIR-20493 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request to stop the validator from appending the FHIR release version, such as |4.0.0, to terminology.fhir.org ValueSet bindings such as the then-current Composition.confidentiality binding to v3-ConfidentialityClassification. A later Jira comment noted an intermediate behavior where the THO version was appended twice.
initial_application: Local git history finds issue-tagged commit 1e00672e608e5357f8d8db1349db0c091031acae, GF#20493: Fix incorrect version appended by validator to terminology.fhir.org value sets. That commit changed the old tools/java ProfileGenerator required-binding version logic. The Jira comment's Git Kindling b400b4b was not present as a current checkout commit, and the old Java tools tree is not present in current HEAD.
additional_context: Composition is active in source/fhir.ini, but current Composition source no longer has Composition.confidentiality and maps CDA confidentiality through Bundle.meta.security. Current Composition terminology.hl7.org ValueSet bindings are unversioned, source-wide searches found no duplicate-pipe or FHIR-release-versioned terminology.hl7.org ValueSet URLs, the linked Zulip thread confirms the issue was validator behavior, and Confluence searches found no conflicting decision record.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current core specification source does not encode the historical invalid versioned terminology ValueSet references, and the only known code-level fix belongs to validator/IG Publisher tooling that is outside the current FHIR source checkout.
